# About This Script

In this phase we are removing phylogenetic signal from traits, using PGLS for continuous traits [Rohlf (2001)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.0014-3820.2001.tb00731.x) and PVR + Binomial GLM for binary traits, based on the [Iserhard et al. (2019)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10531-018-1678-8) procedure. The binary traits are corrected with PVR.bi_sig function developed by us, and is available in "func/" folder. This function is applied for each phylogenetic scenario. 

The final output produces phylogeny-free traits to modelling and the Appendix S13 which is results of the phylogenetic correction for each trait.

> ![WARNING] 
> The creation of the phylogenetic scenarios demands a lot of memory and take a minute to end. Therefore, clear garbage accumulated with `gc()`, the environment and restart the session. You may not be able to run this script if you have less the 8 GB of RAM memory.

# Packages and setup

As usual, multiple packages are required to do run this script, most of them are available on CRAN. Some of then aren't available on CRAN, see below.

```{r}
# .rs.restartR() ## Restart R session
# devtools::install_github("cran/binomTools") # Install binomTools if not yet
rm(list = ls()) ## Clear the R environment
gc() ## Run garbage collection to free up memory

source("func/PVR.bi_sig.R") # Load custom function for binary trait correction
library(rsq) # For R-squared calculations
library(foreach) # For loop abstraction
library(doParallel) # For parallel execution
library(readxl) # For reading Excel files
library(binomTools) # For binomial GLM related tools
library(PVR) # For phylogenetic eigenvector regression
library(ape) # For handling phylogenetic trees
library(phytools) # For phylogenetic analyses
library(dplyr) # For data manipulation
library(nlme) # For PGLS models
library(tidyverse) # Load several packages in the tidyverse
library(openxlsx) 

set.seed(811) ## Set seed for reproducibility
options(scipen = 999) ## Avoid scientific notation in outputs
N = 1000 # Number of trees/replicates to run
```

# Load data

In this step we will need the community matrix and the trait matrix, therefore, we will load the organized dataset.

```{r}
org_data <- readRDS(here("data/org_data.RDS")) # Load dataset with traits and tree tips

trees <- read.tree(here("data/new_ftrees.txt"))[1:N] # Read 1000 phylogenetic trees

org_data$traits <- filter(
  org_data$traits,
  rownames(org_data$traits) %in% trees[[1]]$tip.label
) # Keep only trait data matching tree tips

org_traits <- foreach(i = 1:N) %do%
  {
    org_data$traits[match(trees[[i]]$tip.label, rownames(org_data$traits)), ]
  } # Align traits with each tree tip order
```

# Do parallel computing

As in others scripts we will use parallel computing to hurry to work with the lists and hurry up the process.

```{r}
no_cores <- detectCores() - 4 # Use available cores minus 4 (leave some for system)
registerDoParallel(cores = no_cores) # Register parallel backend
cl <- makeCluster(no_cores, type = "FORK") # Create parallel cluster using FORK
```

# Rhizome Diameter

For Rhizome diameter correction we will use the already well established procedure of PGLS from [Rohlf (2001)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.0014-3820.2001.tb00731.x).

```{r}
fit.pgls <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    nlme::gls(
      model = diam ~ 1,
      data = org_traits[[i]],
      correlation = corBrownian(phy = trees[[i]])
    ) # Fit PGLS model (diameter as response, Brownian correlation)
  }

res.fit.pgls <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    data.frame(diam = residuals(fit.pgls[[i]], type = "normalized")) %>%
      `rownames<-`(rownames(org_traits[[i]])) # Extract normalized residuals from PGLS
  }

S_riz_diam <- res.fit.pgls # Save residuals as phylogenetically corrected trait

S_K_diam <- foreach(i = 1:N, .combine = c, .verbose = T) %dopar%
  {
    phylosig(
      trees[[i]],
      S_riz_diam[[i]]$diam,
      method = "K",
      nsim = 1000,
      test = T
    )$K # Calculate K-statistic (phylogenetic signal)
  }

S_K_diam_P <- foreach(i = 1:N, .combine = c, .verbose = T) %dopar%
  {
    phylosig(
      trees[[i]],
      S_riz_diam[[i]]$diam,
      method = "K",
      nsim = 1000,
      test = T
    )$P # Corresponding p-value for K
  }

S_comp_K <- cbind.data.frame(K = S_K_diam, pvalue = S_K_diam_P) # Combine K and p-values
```

## Saving data

In this step we will save the results of Blomberg's K for each scenario.

```{r}
write.xlsx(
  S_comp_K,
  file = here('outputs/phylogenetic_info/sig_correction.xlsx'),
  startCol = 1,
  startRow = 1
) # Save results to Excel
```


# Binary traits

Now we will start the portion of correction with binary traits, to do so we will use the function
PVR.bi_sig. 

We will repeat the same process for each trait, as following: 
1) Get i-trait at the i-phylogenetic scheme from trait matrix;
2) Run PVR.bi_sig function for the i-trait alongside with the i-phylogenetic scheme.

## Compact Rhizome

```{r}
riz_comp <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    org_traits[[i]][, "r_comp"] %>%
      `names<-`(rownames(org_traits[[i]])) # Extract "r_comp" trait for each tree
  }

 # Correct for phylogenetic signal
riz_comp_correction <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    PVR.bi_sig(t = riz_comp[[i]], # t is a trait vector with binary values
    tree = trees[[i]] # tree is the phylogenetic hypothesis
    )
  }

```

```{r}

riz_cr_correction <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    PVR.bi_sig(t = riz_cr[[i]], tree = trees[[i]])
```


# Output Data 

For the output we must: 

1) Extract the PVR results from the list create by PVR.bi_sig function;
2) Combine into a df.

```{r}
riz_comp_sig <- foreach(i = 1:N) %dopar%
  {
    riz_comp_correction[[i]]$phylo.sig.results # Extract the PVR Results
  } %>%
  map_dfr(.f = cbind, .id = 'trees') # Combine in a data.frame
```

# Save in a list the PVRs pseudo-R2 results (Appendix S13)

We will save and create the Appendix S13.

```{r}
PVR <- vector(mode = "list") #empty list
PVR[[1]] <- riz_comp_sig # add trait to the list
PVR[[2]] <- riz_cr_sig
PVR[[3]] <- riz_lr_sig
PVR[[4]] <- lam_mseg_sig
PVR[[5]] <- buds_sig
PVR[[6]] <- ltri_sig
PVR[[7]] <- ind_sig
PVR[[8]] <- lmorf_sig
PVR[[9]] <- chl_sig

# vector with traits names
names <- c(
  "riz_comp",
  "riz_cr",
  "riz_lr",
  "lam_mseg",
  "buds",
  "ltri",
  "ind",
  "lmorf",
  'chl'
)

# Summarize the results of PVR (mean and range)
PVR_table <- foreach(i = 1:N, j = seq_along(names)) %dopar%
  {
    TABLE_MEAN(PVR[[i]], names[i]) # This is a custom function inside PVR_bi.sig that
    # prepare a summary of PVR results
  } %>%
  list_cbind(name_repair = "unique")
```


# Save PVR data 

```{r}
write.xlsx(
  x = t(PVR_table), # We will transpose the PVR table for consistency
  file = here("outputs/pvr_results.xlsx"),
  startRow = 1,
  startCol = 1,
  keepNA = T,
  rowNames = T
) # 
```
